the introduction of the carbazole moiety in the structure of thiophene-containing alkylidenedimalononitrile derivatives is accompanied by a bathochromic shift of the absorption and emission bands and an increase in the fluorescence intensity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the introduction of carbazole and tri- phenylamine moieties into the structure of the studied chromophores leads to a decrease in the HOMO energy level and an increase in the energy gap between the HOMO and the LUMO levels, which results in a red shift of the absorption band.

the introduction of thiophene and triphenylamines as electron-donor moieties into the push-pull chromogenic systems based on carbazole as the acceptor fragment allows one to achieve a significant increase in the values of the HOMO and the LUMO levels.

the introduction of carbazole and tri- phenylamine moieties into the molecular framework of thiophene-containing alkylidenes leads to an enhancement of the fluorescence intensity, a bathochromic shift of the absorption spectra, and a decrease in the HOMO energy level.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the introduction of the thiophene moiety into the structure of the push-pull chromogenic compounds results in the appearance of new absorption bands in the visible spectral range, and the introduction of the carbazole or triphenylamine fragments into the chromophore structure leads to the appearance of a new band in the near-IR range.
the introduction of the carbazole moiety leads to the bathochromic shift of the absorption and fluorescence bands.

the introduction of thiophene and its oligomers as π-spacers into the structure of carbazole- and phenylamine-containing push-pull compounds leads to a significant increase in the values of the optical band gap (up to 2.8 eV), as well as the values of the HOMO and the LUMO levels (up to -5.3 eV and -2.6 eV, respectively).
